findings.message: Moving settings from the committed config.yaml to pipeline parameters lets anyone who can queue a run override them. `image`, `namespace`, `defaultAgent` and `deadlineMinutes` have no `values:` allowlist in dispatch.yml. Only agent and deadline are validated in `parse_dispatch_args`. `F_IMAGE` and `F_NS` go unvalidated into `kubectl -n` and the rendered Job manifest, so a multi-line value can also inject extra pod-spec fields. Give the parameters a `values:` allowlist or restrict who can queue, and validate `F_IMAGE`, `F_NS` and `F_REF` against a strict charset regex (single line, no whitespace or quotes).
findings.scenario: A user with queue permission runs the pipeline manually with image=evil.example/x:1 for a change whose assignee has the fleet:auto tag. Dispatch fetches the assignee's Claude/Codex token, puts it in the Secret, and mounts it into the attacker's image. Before this change the image came from a reviewed commit to config.yaml.

findings.message: Requester-is-assignee consent was safe when a run only dispatched the approval in its own commit range. The pipeline now scans every approved-not-started change on each run, so the requester shortcut covers every pending change assigned to that person, not just the one they pushed. Tie requester consent to the change that triggered the run (for example, only when the requester authored the approving commit), or require fleet:auto for changes the run did not itself approve.
findings.scenario: Alice pushes an unrelated state.json edit to main. Change C is assigned to Alice, was approved by Bob earlier, has no fleet:auto tag and was never dispatched. The run has BUILD_REQUESTEDFOREMAIL=alice, so C is dispatched on Alice's plan without her say.

findings.message: `F_AZDO_CONFIG="$(cat config.yaml 2>/dev/null || true)"` turns a missing or unreadable config.yaml into an empty mapping, and dispatch carries on. The old code failed closed here, and the tests for that were deleted. AC11 now asserts that dispatch works with no config.yaml. The whole file is also copied into the Job env, where it is readable via `kubectl get job`; the old code passed only the azdo block. Fail when the file cannot be read, and pass only the azdo block.
findings.scenario: config.yaml is unreadable or absent on the pipeline checkout. Dispatch succeeds with an empty FLEET_AZDO_CONFIG, the pod has no state mapping, and the work item stays at Dispatched or Running with no error surfaced.

findings.message: The idempotency record (the fleet:dispatched tag) is written after the Job exists and is only warned about if it fails. The `already_handled` read-then-act is not an atomic claim. `batch: true` serialises only pipeline runs, not a manual `specclaw-fleet dispatch` running alongside one. There is no race test. Claim before creating the Job (a deterministic Job name so a second create gets AlreadyExists, or tag first and abort on failure), and also check for an existing Job for the change.
findings.scenario: The ADO PATCH for the tag returns 412 or a transient 5xx after the Job is created. The code warns and exits 0, the next push to main re-dispatches the same change, and a second Job spends the assignee's plan and opens a second PR. Likewise, a pipeline run and a manual dispatch both read no tag and both create Jobs.

findings.message: The page merge passes the accumulated history and each page as python argv (`"$all" "$page"`), and its exit status is not checked. A single argument over about 128 KB fails with E2BIG on Linux, and the failure leaves `all` empty with no message. A real 200-update page (revisedBy identity objects) is well above that. Merge via stdin or a temp file and add `|| die` to every step. The new tests use `{"id":i}` stubs, so they never exercise realistic page sizes or the exactly-200 boundary.
findings.scenario: A work item with more than about 130 updates of about 1 KB each. The merge python fails with Argument list too long, `all` becomes empty, and the final print fails with an unhelpful JSON error. `auto_tagged_by` fails, so the consent path refuses, tags fleet:refused and marks the item Failed for a healthy work item.

findings.message: The not-approved-at-ref recheck (entrypoint.sh:67) is a fail-closed branch with one test row: status=draft. The `2>/dev/null` and `// empty` paths are untested. Add rows for state.json missing at the ref, truncated or non-object JSON, `.phases.proposal` absent, and status `none`/`approved ` variants. Each should record not-approved-at-ref and never reach `run_agent`.
findings.scenario: If the jq guard were weakened (for example, if the status test were removed from the `||` condition), a ref whose state.json is missing or malformed would still run the agent, and no test would fail.

findings.message: This diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet and plugins/specclaw-sync (new `tag` subcommand, paged `updates`, dispatch behaviour) but touches no `plugin.json` or `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` version. All claude and codex plugin.json files and every marketplace.json entry must carry the same bumped version. If an earlier commit on this branch already bumped all of them, ignore this.
findings.scenario: The fleet and sync changes are merged with versions unchanged. Installed users stay on the old version and never receive the new `tag` subcommand or dispatch behaviour.

findings.message: The `^[0-9]{1,3}$` check still lets a value through that bash arithmetic misreads or that wraps. A leading-zero value such as `08` or `010` is parsed as octal (`08` errors, `010` becomes 8). Values 256-999 wrap modulo 256 on `exit`. Use `10#$rc` in the arithmetic and clamp to 0-255 (or reject greater than 255). The variant test covers only 4-digit and non-numeric payloads, and only the claude path.
findings.scenario: The agent writes `256` to status/exit. Write-back runs `exit 256`, which is exit 0, so a failed run reports success. Writing `08` makes the arithmetic error.
